doc: The Universal Trace. Single source of truth for the contract between execution adapters and visualization renderers. Generated artifacts live in ../generated and are never hand-edited. Normative prose: .kiro/specs/flow-view/trace-schema.md

Profile.doc: Deployment profile that produced the trace.

RunStatus.doc: How the run ended. Every status other than ok/error means the trace is truncated but still valid and replayable.

BranchKind.doc: Syntactic construct that made a control-flow decision.

BranchOutcome.doc: Which way control actually went. Derived from observed execution, never by re-evaluating the condition.

FrameKind.doc: Nature of a call frame. 'library' marks an opaque call whose interior is deliberately not traced.

ObjKind.doc: Renderer hint for a heap object. Describes representation, not semantics.

ObjSetOp.doc: Kind of mutation. Distinguishes replacing element 3 from inserting at 3, which animate differently.

StdinSource.doc: Whether input came from a human at run time or was supplied up front. Measured from how long the read blocked, not assumed.

MetricName.doc: Counters surfaced in the metrics view.

Shape.doc: Inferred data structure shape. Advisory; always user-overridable. 'unknown' renders as a generic object graph.

Confidence.doc: How much to trust an inference.

NoteLevel.doc: Severity of an adapter diagnostic shown to the user.

Value.doc: A value held by a variable or heap slot. Never a nested object: aggregates are referenced by id so that aliasing and cycles are representable, and so mutating a shared object is one event rather than many.
Value.discriminator_note: Exactly one variant key must be present.

prim.doc: An immediate value. Integers outside IEEE-754 safe range are strings with bigint set. NaN and infinities are the strings 'nan', 'inf', '-inf'.
null, bool, int, float, or string.

bigint.doc: Set when prim is a string carrying an integer too large for a double.

truncated.doc: Full original length, when a long string was shortened.

ref.doc: A reference to a heap object.

unavailable.doc: The runtime could not report this value. Deliberate: an honest gap beats a fabricated number.

Arg.doc: One argument at a call site.

SourceFile.doc: A source file participating in the run.

Limits.doc: Resource bounds applied to the run. Present so the UI can explain a truncated trace.

Session.doc: Trace header. Sent once, before any events.

guards_active.doc: Sandbox guards actually in force on this platform. The UI reports these verbatim rather than implying protection that is not present.

StackEntry.doc: One line of a rendered stack trace.

CollapseEffect.doc: Net before/after state for one slot touched inside a folded span. This is what makes a collapse event invertible.

key.doc: Variable name, or heap key rendered as a string.

FrameState.doc: A frame as captured in a snapshot.

ObjectState.doc: A heap object as captured in a snapshot.

slots.doc: Key (index or field, rendered as a string) to value.

order.doc: Explicit slot ordering where it is meaningful, as for lists and arrays.

LoopState.doc: An active loop region as captured in a snapshot.

StateSnapshot.doc: Program state at a point in the trace. Delta-encoded against base_seq unless full is set: a whole-heap snapshot every few hundred steps would outweigh the events it exists to accelerate.

full.doc: True for a keyframe carrying complete state; false for a delta.

base_seq.doc: Snapshot this delta applies to. Absent when full.

removed_frames.doc: Frames gone since base_seq, for deltas.

removed_objects.doc: Objects gone since base_seq, for deltas.

seq.doc: Monotonic from 0. Identity of a point in time.

step.doc: Step ordinal. Present on events the user can land on; absent on bookkeeping events.

path.doc: Source file. Omitted when it is the entry file.

ms.doc: Milliseconds since run start, for the timeline view.

run_end.doc: Always emitted, including on limit breach. A truncated trace is a valid trace.

step_line.doc: Execution arrived at a line. The atom of playback.

branch.doc: A control-flow decision. outcome comes from observed execution; the condition is never re-evaluated, since doing so could fire side effects and change the program being visualized.

expr.doc: Source text of the condition, read from the AST.

result.doc: Evaluated value, only where the runtime surfaces it for free. Null for settrace-based Python. No view may depend on it.

loop_iter.doc: One iteration boundary. Basis for collapsing.

frame_push.doc: A call began. Frame ids are unique for the whole run and never reused, so recursion yields a distinct frame per depth.

var_set.doc: A variable was bound or rebound. prev is what it held before, which is what makes the event invertible.

prev.doc: Absent when the name did not previously exist.

var_del.doc: A binding disappeared: scope exit, explicit delete, block end.

obj_new.doc: A heap object came into existence.

addr.doc: Real address for C/C++; absent for managed languages.

obj_set.doc: A slot of a heap object changed.

key.doc: Index for sequences; field name or map key otherwise.

obj_resize.doc: Bulk length change: clear, extend, array reallocation.

cleared.doc: Keys removed by the resize, so the event stays invertible.

cleared_values.doc: Values those keys held, positionally aligned with cleared.

obj_free.doc: Explicit deallocation. C/C++ only; managed languages do not report collection.

ptr_set.doc: A pointer was retargeted. dangling is the highest-value teaching signal in C: it is what draws the broken arrow explaining a use-after-free.

stdout.doc: Standard output, attributed to the step that produced it.

stderr.doc: Standard error, attributed to the step that produced it.

stdin_response.doc: Input that was supplied. Recorded so replay is deterministic without a human. waited_ms is how long the program actually sat on the read, and is what source is derived from.

exception_uncaught.doc: An exception terminated the program. Terminal, but the trace stays replayable.

metric.doc: Counter increment for the metrics view.

structure_hint.doc: Inferred shape of an object. Advisory, overridable, and carries its evidence so a wrong guess is explainable rather than mysterious.

evidence.doc: Human-readable reasons, shown in the UI.

root.doc: True when this object is the entry point of the structure.

snapshot.doc: Periodic state capture bounding how far a seek must replay.

collapse.doc: A folded span of repeated loop iterations, represented as one composite invertible step. Carries net before/after state so folding cannot break the invertibility guarantee.

note.doc: Adapter diagnostic surfaced to the user, such as a step budget being reached or a frame whose locals could not be read.
